messages:
jules: CI started failing after we switched to pytest-xdist. Tests that used TestClient for sync endpoints now blow up with 'RuntimeError: cannot run the event loop while another loop is running' or sometimes 'attached to a different loop'.
ranjit: Oof. Can you paste a minimal repro and traceback?
jules: Minimal gist:

```
# service/__init__.py
import httpx
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
client = httpx.AsyncClient()  # created at import

@app.get('/health')
async def health():
    r = await client.get('https://example.com')
    return {'ok': r.status_code}
```

```
# tests/test_health.py
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from service import app

def test_health():
    with TestClient(app) as c:
        resp = c.get('/health')
        assert resp.status_code == 200
```
Traceback (snip):
RuntimeError: This event loop is already running.
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/httpx/_async/client.py", line 174, in request
    await self._transport.request(...)
RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
or
RuntimeError: Task <Task pending name='Task-5' ...> attached to a different loop
```
maya: I bet this is the FastAPI TestClient spinning up the ASGI app in a thread with its own loop while the AsyncClient was created on main test loop. TestClient uses anyio to manage threads/loops. Creating AsyncClient at import binds it to whichever loop was current at import time -> mismatch.
jules: Repro is flaky locally but consistent in CI (xdist parallelism makes it worse). We see both: 'attached to a different loop' when worker threads run, and 'event loop is closed' when test runner tears down a loop while the client's background tasks are still pending.
ranjit: Workarounds: (1) create AsyncClient in startup event and store on app.state, (2) use httpx.AsyncClient with transport configured to be thread-safe, (3) switch health handler to use sync httpx.Client inside TestClient. But these are all awkward for library users.
maya: Another option: lazy-init the client using a function that checks asyncio.get_running_loop() at first use and binds then. But that still needs proper aclose on app shutdown.
ci-bot: flaky-tests/job/897 failed: tests/test_health.py::test_health 1 failed (link: https://ci.example/897)
docs: Good catch. We should add a note in SDK docs: "do not instantiate AsyncClient at module import; prefer app-lifespan or per-request context managers especially when using TestClient/xdist". Also add sample snippet showing pattern with app.add_event_handler.
ranjit: For the SDK, propose adding a simple helper factory: `redwood.sdk.make_lifespan_client(app)` which returns an object that will create the AsyncClient during startup and close on shutdown. Include type hints so mypy/pyright users don't get confused about Async vs sync usage.
jules: I'll open a tiny PR in dev-samples that replaces module-scope clients in our examples and adds a test that runs TestClient under xdist (single node) to ensure no loop mismatches.
maya: We should also add a pytest-plugin check that fails if someone imports an AsyncClient at module scope in tests (heuristic: scan files for "httpx.AsyncClient(" outside functions). Might be noisy but useful for CI.
ranjit: Note: Python 3.11 changed some loop handling which made previously latent races surface. We should call this out in the migration doc.
docs: Action items: (1) jules PR for samples (P1), (2) docs to add a section about TestClient/xdist loop mismatches and sample fixes (P2), (3) ranjit to prototype `make_lifespan_client` with type stubs (P2).
jules: Added issue #4021 with repro link and marked P1. Will include CI failing job link. Thanks all.
summary: Tests fail under pytest-xdist/TestClient when AsyncClient is instantiated at module import: loop mismatches and 'event loop is closed' errors. Team recommends lifespan-managed clients, lazy-init helpers, doc updates, and a samples PR to replace module-scope AsyncClient usage.
